title: Sporting CP 2-2 Manchester United: Lammens howler gifts Suarez late equaliser
subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutSporting CP 2-2 Manchester United: Lammens howler gifts Suarez late equaliserShareIn a game that had everything, Sporting CP came from behind to snatch a late draw, though Manchester United had a late winner disallowed.A Senne Lammens mistake gifted Sporting CP a late equaliser as they came from behind to draw 2-2 with Manchester United in a dramatic Champions League encounter.

The first half was a tale of two penalties as Luis Suarez saw his first effort saved by Lammens, who could not get down to the Colombian's next strike after the United goalkeeper gave away another spot-kick.

Bruno Fernandes' return to Estadio Jose Alvalade saw him score a second-half brace, including another penalty, but Suarez pounced on Lammens' error before United had a late winner ruled out and saw Youri Tielemans dismissed.
The game burst into life in the 29th minute when Lisandro Martinez's trailing leg caught Geny Catamo to give away a penalty, but Lammens was equal to Suarez's poor spot-kick straight down the middle.
Less than 90 seconds later, Lammens was involved in more penalty drama as he rushed off his line and wiped out Maxi Araujo.
Suarez stepped up again from 12 yards and took a more confident approach, picking out the bottom-left corner in the 33rd minute, despite Lammens diving the right way once more.

Five minutes before the break, Amad Diallo thought he had an equaliser; he latched onto Tielemans' throughball and hit the crossbar before heading in the follow-up, but the referee's whistle went before the ball crossed the line for a foul by the Belgian midfielder.
Amad fizzed wide just before the break, and United started the second half on top, with Martinez clumsily bundled over by Eduardo Quaresma as a third penalty was awarded.
Fernandes confidently stepped up, slotting into the bottom-left corner to pull United level in the 48th minute against his former side.
He doubled his tally in comical fashion two minutes later. With no options around him, Fernandes tried a long-distance strike that hit a divot and flew over the stunned Kaique.

On a hat-trick, Fernandes then sent a free-kick wide of the right post, but it was Lammens who found himself in the spotlight again at the other end as he failed to catch a looping Ivan Fresnada cross under pressure from Suarez, who acrobatically finished into the empty net with 10 minutes remaining.

There was more drama two minutes later as a Fernandes corner was spilled by Kaique and Sporting could not clear it off the line, but after a trip to the VAR monitor, the referee ruled out the goal as Patrick Dorgu was adjudged to have fouled the goalkeeper.

United finished the game with 10 men as Tielemans was sent off for two bookable offences; he caught Sergi Altimira late in the 93rd minute, receiving the visitors' fifth red card in all competitions this season.
Fine margins leave Pochettino still chasing first win
It was a big game for both managers, with Paulo Fonseca and Mauricio Pochettino both taking charge of their first European game with their new clubs, and it is the former who will be happier.

There were positive signs for United in the early stages, as this marked the first time since October 31 against Chelsea that they have not conceded in the first 15 minutes of a game in all competitions.

But four minutes of madness threatened to send them spiralling; they have now conceded a penalty in four of their last five matches, though Lammens saved his first for United on what was his eighth attempt – only for him to be punished moments later.

If anyone was going to save the Red Devils, it was going to be their captain. Fernandes has 30 goal involvements in all competitions in 2026 (12 goals, 18 assists) – only Erling Haaland has more (27 goals, five assists) among Premier League players.
It is also only the second time he has scored two goals in a Champions League match (also in November 2020 versus Istanbul Basaksehir).

But United's recent struggles came back to haunt them again as more mistakes crept into their game, with Lammens and Tielemans the biggest signs of that. They have conceded the most goals in all competitions among teams in Europe's top-five leagues (36).
